commands.purpose: Simulate a partially-migrated DB that retains the legacy 5-arg hybrid_search and REAL-typed decay_unused_priorities overloads alongside the current 8-arg/float8 versions, prove the orphan causes an ambiguous-call error, then prove the hardened bootstrap removes the orphans (finding #1).
commands.observed_result: With both overloads present, 'SELECT count(*) FROM hybrid_search('x', NULL::vector, 5, 60, NULL)' failed with: ERROR: function hybrid_search(unknown, vector, integer, integer, unknown) is not unique. (The decay_unused_priorities(0, 0.9) numeric-literal call did NOT error because Postgres prefers the float8 (double precision) candidate, but the stale float4/REAL overload still lingered as an orphan.) After re-running the hardened bootstrap, pg_proc shows exactly one overload of each: hybrid_search(text,vector,integer,integer,integer,text,jsonb,text) and decay_unused_priorities(integer,double precision); the previously-ambiguous hybrid_search(...) 5-positional-arg call now returns count 0 (no error).
